summary.text: The evidence suggests licorice gargling before surgery likely reduces sore throat after a breathing tube, but the answer is not fully certain.
Our estimate from trial data found a 13.7 percentage point lower risk of sore throat with licorice, with a 95% confidence interval from 26.3 to 1.2 percentage points lower.
Several published studies also report lower sore throat rates or severity with licorice gargle compared with sugar-water or water.
However, the best studies point in different directions, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

comparison.text: Our adjusted estimate of a 13.7 percentage point reduction is consistent in direction with published results showing licorice lowered sore throat rates, such as 19% versus 36% at 30 minutes and 10% versus 35% at 1.5 hours.

The data were treated as observational, and the key assumption is no unmeasured confounding after adjusting for nothing.
The best studies point in different directions, lowering certainty to moderate.

Our estimate from trial data found a 13.7 percentage point lower risk of sore throat with licorice, with a 95% confidence interval from 26.3 to 1.2 percentage points lower. [res-42d266b4] Several published studies also report lower sore throat rates or severity with licorice gargle compared with sugar-water or water.
